Today, IndianOil, BPCL and HPCL have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Saudi Aramco, a leading global integrated energy and chemicals company in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, to jointly develop and build the said project. The partnership would bring together the crude supply, resources, technologies, experiences, and expertise of these multiple oil companies with an established commercial presence around the world. Saudi Aramco may also bring in a strategic partner to co-invest in the project. The MOU would provide for the joint ownership, control and management of the refinery project. The refinery will be capable of processing 60 MMTPA Crude Oil i.e. 1.2 million barrels of crude oil per day (of which some will be Arabian crude) and produce a range of refined petroleum products, including Motor Spirit and Diesel, which will meet Euro VI fuel specifications. It will also provide feedstock for the integrated petrochemical complex, which will be capable of producing approximately 18 million tons per annum of petrochemical products.  The project would rank among the world��s largest refining and petrochemicals projects and will be designed to meet India��s fast-growing fuels and petrochemicals demand.  '.

This is with reference to news item dated November 13, 2014 captioned "Indian Oil Corporation board okays Ennore LNG terminal". The Company has submitted its clarification to captioned news on November 14, 2014. The Company has further clarified as follows:   1) The LNG project at Ennore is to be implemented through a Joint Venture Company and not directly by Indian Oil. The equity participation in the JV company is proposed as under:-  Indian Oil : 45%  TIDCO : 5%  (A Tamil Nadu State Govt. Enterprise)  Balance 50% by financial institutions.   2) The JVC will be initially incorporated with a Seed Capital of Rs. 1 lacs by aforesaid JV partners out of which IndianOil s investment would only be Rs. 45,000/- at present.  3) As the project activities progress, the strategic Joint Venture Partners would be identified and inducted as Equity Partners.  4) The project related activities are yet to commence.  Considering the above we would like to state that, at present, the project is not materially significant, keeping in view the financials of the Corporation with a turnover over Rs. 4,50,000 crore.  We would like to confirm that any significant and material development would be notified to the exchange immediately upon its occurrence, in accordance with the provisions of the Listing Agreement.

attchmntText: Indian Oil Corporation Limited has informed the Exchange that Indian Oil Corporation Limited (IOCL) through its wholly owned affiliate IndOil Montney Ltd, Canada have signed transaction agreements with Progress Energy Canada Ltd. (Progress Energy Canada), PETRONAS Carigali Canada BV (PCC BV) wholly owned affiliates of Petroliam Nasional Berhad (PETRONAS) for the acquisition of a 10% interest in Progress Energy Canada's LNG-destined natural gas reserves in northeast British Columbia and in the proposed Pacific Northwest LNG Ltd. (PNW LNG) export facility on Canada's West Coast. As part of the transaction, IOCL shall also offtake 1.2 million tons of liquefied natural gas (LNG) per annum, which represents 10% of the LNG facility's production, for a minimum period of 20 years. JAPEX Montney Ltd. with 10% and Petroleum BRUNEI with 3% are the other partners who acquired their interest in the project in 2013. PETRONAS will hold the remaining 77% of the integrated project.

Indian Oil Corporation Ltd has informed the Exchange that on October 29, 2004 there was a loud explosion in the Reactor of the FCC Unit of Gujarat Refinery followed by major fire. The fire was controlled and fully extinguished within two hours of occurrence. Extensive damages appear to have been caused to the Reactor section of the Unit and consequently the FCC Unit has been shutdown. There was no casualty. Separate team from IndianOil and EIL have been deployed to the Refinery to plan repairs/restoration work. It is anticipated based on preliminary estimates that the restoration work is likely to take about a month's time. However, the maintenance of supply line would not be in any way affected as the company has sufficient inventories as well as sufficient logistic plan for supply and distribution of petroleum products.
